mcq_fix.s: Annamacharya (1408-1503) is associated with the patronage of which Vijayanagara ruler, who was his contemporary?
mcq_fix.why: as worded, Devaraya I (r. 1406-22) was also a contemporary; ambiguous

mcq_drop.why: dubious: 'first recruitment of Muslims' is usually credited to Devaraya II (APPSC 2011 key: 10,000 Muslim soldiers); sources conflict

patterns: Bulk of PYQs are one-liners: founders Harihara and Bukka (1336), Tungabhadra dam = Devaraya I, Abdur Razzaq = Devaraya II, embassy to China = Bukka I.
APPSC-specific: founders as Kakatiya officials (Warangal link), Raichur Doab as main cause of wars, Devaraya II's literary hall Mutyalasala, 'odd one out' dynasties.
Dynasty order Sangama-Saluva-Tuluva-Aravidu and the usurpations (Saluva Narasimha, Vira Narasimha) are a frequent statement item.
Literary sources (Madhura Vijayam by Gangadevi, Sayana's Vedic commentaries, Sewell's A Forgotten Empire) recur.
App adds deep Andhra-campaign detail (Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam, Draksharama inscription) and origin-theory scholars beyond PYQ depth, but mostly sound.
